events.name: Total Lunar Eclipse
events.desc: The Moon passes fully through Earth's umbral shadow, turning a deep coppery red.

events.name: Partial Solar Eclipse
events.desc: The Moon partially covers the Sun's disk, visible from parts of the Southern Hemisphere.

events.name: Total Solar Eclipse
events.desc: A rare total solar eclipse crossing Greenland, Iceland and Spain.

events.name: Partial Lunar Eclipse
events.desc: The Moon dips partly into Earth's umbral shadow.

events.name: Annular Solar Eclipse
events.desc: The Moon appears too small to fully cover the Sun, leaving a bright "ring of fire".

events.name: Total Lunar Eclipse
events.desc: A total lunar eclipse turning the Moon a deep red.

events.name: Total Solar Eclipse
events.desc: One of the longest total solar eclipses of the century, crossing Spain, North Africa and the Middle East.

events.name: Quadrantids Meteor Shower Peak
events.desc: A short, sharp peak producing up to 110 meteors/hour under ideal skies.

events.name: Lyrids Meteor Shower Peak
events.desc: Fast, bright meteors from debris of Comet Thatcher.

events.name: Eta Aquariids Meteor Shower Peak
events.desc: Debris from Halley's Comet, best seen from the tropics and Southern Hemisphere.

events.name: Delta Aquariids Meteor Shower Peak
events.desc: A moderate shower best viewed from the Southern Hemisphere and tropics.

events.name: Perseids Meteor Shower Peak
events.desc: One of the best showers of the year, from debris of Comet Swift-Tuttle.

events.name: Orionids Meteor Shower Peak
events.desc: Fast meteors from debris of Halley's Comet.

events.name: Leonids Meteor Shower Peak
events.desc: Fast meteors, occasionally producing storms in cyclical years.

events.name: Geminids Meteor Shower Peak
events.desc: The most reliable and prolific shower of the year, from asteroid 3200 Phaethon.

events.name: March Equinox
events.desc: The Sun crosses the celestial equator; day and night are nearly equal worldwide.

events.name: June Solstice
events.desc: The Sun reaches its northernmost point — the longest day in the Northern Hemisphere.

events.name: September Equinox
events.desc: The Sun crosses the celestial equator heading south.

events.name: December Solstice
events.desc: The Sun reaches its southernmost point — the shortest day in the Northern Hemisphere.

events.name: Jupiter at Opposition
events.desc: Jupiter is opposite the Sun in our sky, rising at sunset and visible all night at its brightest.

events.name: Saturn at Opposition
events.desc: Saturn is closest and brightest, ideal for viewing its rings through a telescope.

events.name: Venus at Greatest Elongation
events.desc: Venus reaches its greatest apparent distance from the Sun, shining brilliantly at dusk.
